pathway.title: OLIN Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage has risen while earnings fell. Trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell by USD 115.2 million to USD 536.6 million between FY2025 and Q3 2026 (a fall of 17.7 percent), while reported total debt rose by USD 185.8 million to USD 3,013.1 million and cash rose by USD 47.2 million, so net debt rose by USD 138.6 million to USD 2,798.3 million. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.08x to 5.21x, total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 4.34x to 5.62x and cash interest cover from 3.66x to 3.15x (Documentary Fact; CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that fixed interest and capital costs are carried by a smaller EBITDA base, and the implication is less tolerance for further operating shocks before covenant relief ends. The ratios use the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which excludes restructuring, acquisition-related costs, the legacy litigation charge of the first quarter of 2026 and, on the CP-1 reproduction, the FY2025 Shintech charge; the covenant ratio is defined differently and its levels are not supplied.

Second, the earnings decline is concentrated in Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls. Segment income for the nine months of 2026 was USD 80.2 million against USD 270.8 million, with the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage costing USD 72.2 million, lower volumes USD 55.3 million, lower pricing USD 42.0 million and a legacy litigation charge USD 36.1 million, partly offset by USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). Winchester segment income was USD 77.1 million and Epoxy USD 13.7 million for the nine months, against USD 67.1 million and a loss of USD 84.3 million a year earlier. The mechanism is operating leverage in a commodity chlor alkali segment that holds most of the depreciation base; the implication is that recovery of credit metrics depends on that segment normalising after the outage, which management says is restored (Management Language), and on epoxy demand, which the filing describes as weak.

Third, cash generation is uneven. Nine month operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million did not cover capital spending of USD 106.6 million, leaving free cash flow before dividends of USD -36.9 million and, after dividends of USD 68.3 million, USD -105.2 million. Trailing twelve month free cash flow was USD 221.5 million, or USD 130.4 million after trailing dividends of USD 91.1 million, because the fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced USD 321.2 million of operating cash flow (Documentary Fact; derived from CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is working capital and timing: receivables rose USD 133.4 million on third quarter sales timing. The implication is that fourth quarter 2026 working capital release, not earnings alone, determines whether net debt falls by year end.

Fourth, liquidity is adequate and maturities are not near. Cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn revolver gives USD 1,244.4 million, equal to 2.68 times the USD 465.0 million receivables facility maturing November 19, 2027, the first maturity. The revolver and term loan mature March 14, 2030 and no covenant limited borrowing at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that the nearest wall is small against liquidity, but the 2029 notes of USD 669.3 million and 2030 maturities of USD 1,213.4 million together are USD 1,882.7 million, or 62.1 percent of USD 3,030.7 million principal. The implication is that refinancing risk sits in 2029 and 2030 and depends on market access.

Fifth, covenant relief and ranking mechanics are time-limited. The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed the net leverage and coverage covenants, added subsidiary guarantees and collateral for the bank facilities, and limits debt, non-regular distributions and asset sales until the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff). Numeric levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. The mechanism is that bank debt of USD 1,163.1 million (38.4 percent of principal, comprising the term loan, drawn revolver and receivables facility) has collateral or receivables security during relief, while the senior notes of USD 1,784.6 million (58.9 percent) have security not stated in the pack; the implication is that creditor priority changes when relief ends, and the notes' position cannot be assessed without the indentures. This is a mechanic, not a recovery conclusion.

Sixth, the Huntsman merger replaces uncertainty with a different one. The all-stock merger is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, with a new USD 2,500.0 million facility replacing Olin's bank facilities and Huntsman's revolver (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). The mechanism is a reset of covenants, collateral, amortisation and pricing, with Huntsman obligations joining the guarantor group; the implication is that existing Olin creditors will hold claims on a combined company whose leverage cannot be computed because Huntsman financials, debt and synergy targets are not in the pack. Ratings reflect this: Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, S&P BB on Credit Watch Developing and Moody's Ba2 with a Negative outlook.

Seventh, claims outside reported debt are moderate but real: operating lease liabilities of USD 387.8 million, an environmental reserve of USD 156.8 million, a net balance sheet pension position of USD 63.6 million (accrued pension liability USD 196.5 million less pension assets USD 132.9 million) with a foreign plan deficit of USD 204.2 million at December 31, 2025, and the Shintech judgment on which about USD 114 million was paid in the nine months (CP-1 handoff). The implication is claims that rank alongside financial debt in cash terms but sit outside the debt ratios.

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity runway is the first strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver against a nearest maturity of USD 465.0 million, with no covenant restricting borrowing at September 30, 2026. Business diversification is the second (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff): three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales, a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics, and a Winchester business with government contract revenue of about 13 percent of 2025 sales that improved to USD 77.1 million of segment income over the nine months. Third, covenant relief was obtained in February 2026 with the revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 maintained, and Olin reports compliance with no event of default (Documentary Fact). Fourth, issuer behaviour shows no creditor-adverse transfer: there were no buybacks in the nine months of 2026 after USD 50.5 million in 2025 and no priming or collateral release is documented, though the pack is limited (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, structural cost actions are cited by management as lowering operating costs, and the nine month Chlor Alkali bridge shows USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Management Language qualified by Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Leverage is elevated and rising: net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.21x and total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.62x, with cover at 3.15x (Documentary Fact). Earnings are concentrated in a segment hit by an operating outage and by weaker pricing and volumes, and the outage impact in the third quarter of USD 32.1 million exceeded the July estimate of about USD 20 million (Documentary Fact). Epoxy remains challenged by subsidised Asian competition and weak demand (Documentary Fact). Free cash flow for the nine months was negative while the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend was maintained, so dividends of USD 68.3 million were covered by net borrowing (Analyst Interpretation). Ratings were lowered in February 2026 to BB+, Ba2 and BB and now carry mixed watch and outlook signals (Documentary Fact). Fourth quarter guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million implies a seasonally weak quarter, with management citing destocking, higher feedstock costs, Asian export pressure and turnarounds (Management Language). Finally, the credit depends on covenant levels, ranking and merger terms that the pack does not contain (Insufficient Information).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On June 15, 2026 Olin entered into a definitive agreement with Huntsman Corporation for an all-stock merger of equals to form OlinHuntsman Corporation; each Huntsman share converts into 0.5476 Olin shares, and Olin holders are expected to own approximately 54.5% and Huntsman holders approximately 45.5% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:8). Shareholders of both companies approved the proposals on August 25, 2026 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired, but remaining regulatory approvals and customary conditions are outstanding and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, having been expected in the first half of 2027 in the July release (10-Q Q3 page:8; EX-99.1 Q2 page:3). The registration statement on Form S-4/A was declared effective on July 13, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:58). Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million, and the Q2 2026 10-Q adds reimbursement of Huntsman expenses of up to USD 30 million (10-Q Q2 page:56). Olin booked acquisition-related costs of USD 13.7 million in Q3 2026 and USD 24.3 million in the nine months and expects USD 35 million to USD 40 million for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:45). The merger agreement restricts certain Olin actions without Huntsman's consent before closing (10-Q Q3 page:57).

The new debt is the OlinHuntsman Credit Facility of USD 2,500.0 million under a second amendment dated October 27, 2026 to Olin's credit agreement, effective on the merger Closing Date subject to closing and customary conditions. It has a term loan of USD 750.0 million replacing Olin's existing USD 650.0 million term loan facility, and a revolver of USD 1,750.0 million replacing Olin's USD 1,200.0 million revolver and Huntsman's revolver. The term loan amortises at 1.250% per quarter from the first full fiscal quarter after closing through the fourth anniversary quarter, then 1.875% per quarter, and the facility matures five years after the Closing Date. It is guaranteed by certain Olin subsidiaries and certain Huntsman subsidiaries, secured by first priority liens on certain assets, carries a pricing grid on the net leverage ratio, and has covenants on secured debt to EBITDA and on EBITDA to interest expense, with levels not supplied. The term loan is expected to be fully drawn at closing, with proceeds and any revolver loans used to refinance Olin's senior secured facility, repay and terminate Huntsman's revolver and pay fees (10-Q Q3 page:8, page:9). Olin's senior notes of USD 669.3 million, USD 515.3 million and USD 600.0 million and its USD 465.0 million receivables facility are not stated to be refinanced (CP-1 handoff; 10-Q Q3 page:12). No new notes issuance is described. Huntsman's debt, its balance sheet, its amounts under its revolver and the pro forma capital structure are not in the pack, so combined leverage and the net new debt at closing are not calculable.

fields.value: The pack supports a creditor snapshot of OLIN Corp (the Virginia registrant Olin Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries, a single reporting perimeter) at Q3 2026, with limitations, and no consumer is blocked. The filed 10-K and three 10-Qs are original authority for statements, notes, debt, liquidity and segment facts, while the three Exhibit 99.1 releases are attributed management claims that carry the non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA and net debt ratio. Evidence runs from covenant relief narrative (10-Q Q3 page:13, page:50) to a source risk: the numeric maintenance levels, the executed credit agreements and the October 27, 2026 amendments are exhibits incorporated by reference and not supplied, so covenant headroom and the combined-company facility terms rest on summary text. The downstream consequence is that leverage and liquidity can be computed from printed inputs but a covenant-compliance conclusion cannot be tested. Pinned sources contain no Huntsman financials, so only Olin-side merger facts are supported. Readiness for each consumer is set out in the tables below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: OLIN Corp, a vertically integrated chlor alkali, epoxy and ammunition manufacturer, ends Q3 2026 with weaker credit metrics than at FY2025, while liquidity remains adequate and the debt stack has no maturity before the receivables facility in November 2027. The strongest support is liquidity: cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn on the revolver, and a revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 (10-Q Q3 page:13). The weakest point is earnings: company-defined trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA is USD 536.6 million against USD 651.8 million at FY2025 (EX-99.1 Q3 page:11), so reported total debt of USD 3,013.1 million equals 5.62x and net debt equals 5.21x, up from 4.34x and 4.08x. What decides the outcome is fourth quarter 2026 delivery against guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million adjusted EBITDA (EX-99.1 Q3 page:2), the covenant relief that ends by September 30, 2027, and whether the Huntsman merger closes in the first quarter of 2027 with the new USD 2,500.0 million facility (10-Q Q3 page:8). Nine month 2026 free cash flow before dividends was negative, and every ratio below uses the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA unless stated.

fields.value: Stack check: the instruments sum to 3,030.7 before deferred costs and 3,013.1 after, matching the balance sheet (10-Q Q3 page:12). Variable-rate debt is 1,246.1, equal to 528.1 plus 170.0 plus 465.0 plus 83.0 and to the figure in the 10-Q (page:52). Under the October 27, 2026 second amendment, the term loan commitment becomes USD 750.0 million and the revolver USD 1,750.0 million on the merger Closing Date, five year maturity, secured first priority and guaranteed by certain Olin and Huntsman subsidiaries; this is conditional on merger closing and is not yet a debt obligation (10-Q Q3 page:8, page:9).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 214.8 million (10-Q Q3 page:2) plus revolver undrawn commitments of USD 1,029.6 million, which are net of USD 170.0 million drawn and USD 0.4 million of letters of credit on a USD 1,200.0 million facility (10-Q Q3 page:13), giving USD 1,244.4 million. The 2024 Receivables Financing Agreement adds USD 34.0 million of borrowing-base-limited capacity (10-Q Q3 page:15), giving USD 1,278.4 million, consistent with the release's approximately USD 1.3 billion (EX-99.1 Q3 page:3). No covenant limited borrowing at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:14). At December 31, 2025 the leverage covenant limited additional borrowings to USD 825.3 million (10-K page:65). No facility expires within twelve months of September 30, 2026; the receivables facility matures November 19, 2027, so the USD 465.0 million drawn would fall within twelve months of the December 31, 2026 balance sheet date and could then be classified as current unless extended; the filings do not state the classification.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Senior Secured Credit Facility has a maximum net leverage ratio (consolidated total debt net of unrestricted cash over EBITDA, excluding receivables financing borrowings up to USD 425.0 million) and a minimum coverage ratio (EBITDA to interest expense) (10-Q Q3 page:14). The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed both and adjusted the EBITDA and debt definitions for the covenant relief period, which ends on the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (10-K page:140, page:141; 10-Q Q3 page:13). The numeric levels, step-downs and the covenant EBITDA are Not supplied after search of all seven sources, so headroom is Not calculable. Olin states it was in compliance with all covenants at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:14). The filings word the leverage test differently: the 10-K describes secured debt (10-K page:106) while the 10-Q describes consolidated total debt, net of unrestricted cash; the executed agreement would settle this. The company ratio of 5.2x (net debt to adjusted EBITDA, all debt) is not the covenant ratio, because the covenant nets only unrestricted cash and excludes up to USD 425.0 million of receivables financing. An illustrative figure on that definition, using reported debt and company adjusted EBITDA (not the covenant EBITDA), is 4.42x (Calculations). The incoming OlinHuntsman Credit Facility will carry a secured debt to EBITDA and a coverage covenant (10-Q Q3 page:8, page:9); levels Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: OLIN Corp is a publicly listed, sponsor-free manufacturer whose creditor case rests on integrated chlor alkali and epoxy assets plus a defence-linked ammunition business, and whose near-term outcome is set by a single pending transaction: an all-stock merger of equals with Huntsman Corporation, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The strongest support is diversification and integration, with three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales and a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics. The weakest point is the Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls segment, where the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage cut segment income to USD 80.2 million for the nine months from USD 270.8 million. What decides the credit is whether the merger closes, what the combined company borrows under the new USD 2,500.0 million facility, and whether fourth quarter 2026 earnings meet the USD 80 million to USD 100 million guidance, so execution risk on the merger is the main swing factor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On June 15, 2026 Olin entered into a definitive agreement with Huntsman Corporation for an all-stock merger of equals to form OlinHuntsman Corporation; each Huntsman share converts into 0.5476 Olin shares, and Olin holders are expected to own approximately 54.5% and Huntsman holders approximately 45.5% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:8). Shareholders of both companies approved the proposals on August 25, 2026 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired, but remaining regulatory approvals and customary conditions are outstanding and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, having been expected in the first half of 2027 in the July release (10-Q Q3 page:8; EX-99.1 Q2 page:3). Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million, and the Q2 2026 10-Q adds reimbursement of Huntsman expenses of up to USD 30 million (10-Q Q2 page:56). fields.value: OLIN Corp's fundamental credit is weakening but not impaired in the near term: leverage has stepped up while liquidity and the maturity profile give time to reach the Huntsman merger decision point. The strongest support is USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, no maturity before the USD 465.0 million receivables facility in November 2027, and three segments that do not move together. The weakest point is trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 536.6 million, which puts net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 5.21x against 4.08x at FY2025 and cash interest cover at 3.15x. What decides the outcome is fourth quarter 2026 delivery against guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million, closing of the merger in the first quarter of 2027, and the end of covenant relief by September 30, 2027. Confidence is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage has risen while earnings fell. Trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell by USD 115.2 million to USD 536.6 million between FY2025 and Q3 2026 (a fall of 17.7 percent), while reported total debt rose by USD 185.8 million to USD 3,013.1 million and cash rose by USD 47.2 million, so net debt rose by USD 138.6 million to USD 2,798.3 million. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.08x to 5.21x, total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 4.34x to 5.62x and cash interest cover from 3.66x to 3.15x (Documentary Fact; CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that fixed interest and capital costs are carried by a smaller EBITDA base, and the implication is less tolerance for further operating shocks before covenant relief ends. The ratios use the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which excludes restructuring, acquisition-related costs, the legacy litigation charge of the first quarter of 2026 and, on the CP-1 reproduction, the FY2025 Shintech charge; the covenant ratio is defined differently and its levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the earnings decline is concentrated in Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls. Segment income for the nine months of 2026 was USD 80.2 million against USD 270.8 million, with the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage costing USD 72.2 million, lower volumes USD 55.3 million, lower pricing USD 42.0 million and a legacy litigation charge USD 36.1 million, partly offset by USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). Winchester segment income was USD 77.1 million and Epoxy USD 13.7 million for the nine months, against USD 67.1 million and a loss of USD 84.3 million a year earlier. The mechanism is operating leverage in a commodity chlor alkali segment that holds most of the depreciation base; the implication is that recovery of credit metrics depends on that segment normalising after the outage, which management says is restored (Management Language), and on epoxy demand, which the filing describes as weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, cash generation is uneven. Nine month operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million did not cover capital spending of USD 106.6 million, leaving free cash flow before dividends of USD -36.9 million and, after dividends of USD 68.3 million, USD -105.2 million. Trailing twelve month free cash flow was USD 221.5 million, or USD 130.4 million after trailing dividends of USD 91.1 million, because the fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced USD 321.2 million of operating cash flow (Documentary Fact; derived from CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is working capital and timing: receivables rose USD 133.4 million on third quarter sales timing. The implication is that fourth quarter 2026 working capital release, not earnings alone, determines whether net debt falls by year end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, liquidity is adequate and maturities are not near. Cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn revolver gives USD 1,244.4 million, equal to 2.68 times the USD 465.0 million receivables facility maturing November 19, 2027, the first maturity. The revolver and term loan mature March 14, 2030 and no covenant limited borrowing at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that the nearest wall is small against liquidity, but the 2029 notes of USD 669.3 million and 2030 maturities of USD 1,213.4 million together are USD 1,882.7 million, or 62.1 percent of USD 3,030.7 million principal. The implication is that refinancing risk sits in 2029 and 2030 and depends on market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, covenant relief and ranking mechanics are time-limited. The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed the net leverage and coverage covenants, added subsidiary guarantees and collateral for the bank facilities, and limits debt, non-regular distributions and asset sales until the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff). Numeric levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. The mechanism is that bank debt of USD 1,163.1 million (38.4 percent of principal, comprising the term loan, drawn revolver and receivables facility) has collateral or receivables security during relief, while the senior notes of USD 1,784.6 million (58.9 percent) have security not stated in the pack; the implication is that creditor priority changes when relief ends, and the notes' position cannot be assessed without the indentures. This is a mechanic, not a recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the Huntsman merger replaces uncertainty with a different one. The all-stock merger is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, with a new USD 2,500.0 million facility replacing Olin's bank facilities and Huntsman's revolver (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). The mechanism is a reset of covenants, collateral, amortisation and pricing, with Huntsman obligations joining the guarantor group; the implication is that existing Olin creditors will hold claims on a combined company whose leverage cannot be computed because Huntsman financials, debt and synergy targets are not in the pack. Ratings reflect this: Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, S&P BB on Credit Watch Developing and Moody's Ba2 with a Negative outlook.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, claims outside reported debt are moderate but real: operating lease liabilities of USD 387.8 million, an environmental reserve of USD 156.8 million, a net balance sheet pension position of USD 63.6 million (accrued pension liability USD 196.5 million less pension assets USD 132.9 million) with a foreign plan deficit of USD 204.2 million at December 31, 2025, and the Shintech judgment on which about USD 114 million was paid in the nine months (CP-1 handoff). The implication is claims that rank alongside financial debt in cash terms but sit outside the debt ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity runway is the first strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver against a nearest maturity of USD 465.0 million, with no covenant restricting borrowing at September 30, 2026. Business diversification is the second (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff): three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales, a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics, and a Winchester business with government contract revenue of about 13 percent of 2025 sales that improved to USD 77.1 million of segment income over the nine months. Third, covenant relief was obtained in February 2026 with the revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 maintained, and Olin reports compliance with no event of default (Documentary Fact). Fourth, issuer behaviour shows no creditor-adverse transfer: there were no buybacks in the nine months of 2026 after USD 50.5 million in 2025 and no priming or collateral release is documented, though the pack is limited (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, structural cost actions are cited by management as lowering operating costs, and the nine month Chlor Alkali bridge shows USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Management Language qualified by Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage is elevated and rising: net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.21x and total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.62x, with cover at 3.15x (Documentary Fact). Earnings are concentrated in a segment hit by an operating outage and by weaker pricing and volumes, and the outage impact in the third quarter of USD 32.1 million exceeded the July estimate of about USD 20 million (Documentary Fact). Epoxy remains challenged by subsidised Asian competition and weak demand (Documentary Fact). Free cash flow for the nine months was negative while the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend was maintained, so dividends of USD 68.3 million were covered by net borrowing (Analyst Interpretation). Ratings were lowered in February 2026 to BB+, Ba2 and BB and now carry mixed watch and outlook signals (Documentary Fact). Fourth quarter guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million implies a seasonally weak quarter, with management citing destocking, higher feedstock costs, Asian export pressure and turnarounds (Management Language). Finally, the credit depends on covenant levels, ranking and merger terms that the pack does not contain (Insufficient Information).
